summary: A satirical news-style piece about the supposed arrival of a real Holodeck, unveiled by VirtuReal Solutions CEO Dr. Lana Turing in September 2023. It covers the tech's AI companions, a booming virtual content economy, comic glitches, virtual dating, and skepticism from critics like Eleanor Rigby, closing with a joke that readers may already be inside the Holodeck.
one_line: A humorous news satire on VirtuReal Solutions' Holodeck, covering its launch, virtual economy, glitches, AI relationships and critics.
key_facts: Dr. Lana Turing, CEO of VirtuReal Solutions, unveiled the Holodeck on September 17, 2023 at the FutureTech Symposium, calling it the "Alpha and Omega of virtual escapism".
The Holodeck is a room-sized construct said to simulate anything from a Martian beach stroll to a polar bear hug in the Arctic without frostbite.
VirtuReal Solutions has a proprietary AI named "EmpathyBot" that nods along to users' stories.
Turing said virtual entities can be given the appearance of anyone from history books, celebrity magazines or video games, such as having tea with Cleopatra or arm-wrestling Genghis Khan.

On December 5, 2023, Conrad Hertz, a self-proclaimed "experience connoisseur", declared his three-day Holodeck marathon "more profound than that time I found Nirvana in the depths of a kale smoothie".
A job market for Holodeck content creators has surged, with titles like Virtual World Landscaper and Pixelated Party Planner.
On Gilgamesh Island, a virtual vacation spot, Neo-Baroque Garden Designers and Surrealists Underwater Architects are in a fierce rivalry.
On March 2, 2024, a glitch trapped user Barry Bigglesworth in a 16th-century French court where everyone behaved like cats; his attempt to woo nobility with a can of tuna was streamed live.
An infinite stair glitch left users climbing endless stairs, described as a mix of a mild existential crisis and an intense leg day.
Last Valentine's Day, the most popular hot date was reportedly with AI renditions of literary characters, such as a virtual Lord Byron.

Tech columnist and birdwatcher Eleanor Rigby leads the skeptics, asking why one would roam make-believe meadows when one can see a real sparrow, though she called the mosquito-free swamp "a rather pleasant touch".
Critics call the Holodeck an overpriced screensaver, likened to 90s digital pets without the poop.
